structured_output.world_model:
W2 (empirical), after E043. Tip is E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. Fresh seeds 13-22 (E038) gave 0.7525. E043 re-ran the same code and read 0.7497 at 5.294 s, so identical code is not reliably bit-identical across rebuilds. Kernel reselection is a plausible cause. Population mean is about 0.752, leaving about 0.2 pp of headroom over the 0.75 bar. The 0.753 gate on seeds 0-2 is a coin flip even for the tip.

Mechanisms, with the experiments behind them:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch, for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 stacked the freeze with +0.5 epoch and saved 0.40 s vs E027 at about 0 pp.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. More than 10 time-neutral boosters failed (E025, E029, E030, E032, wd, LS). Averaging, LR shape and wd sit at a flat optimum within about 0.2 pp.
3. Time tracks pixels. Early low resolution is nearly free up to about 30% at 20 px (E026, E033). E040 (40/0/30/30) cost 0.06 pp. E041 (12-step trim) cost 0.2 pp.
4. Backward truncation on large maps was the best lever (E028, E034, E036). E037 (freeze at 60%) saved 0.25 s but cost 0.38 pp. E039 and E042 saved only 0.03-0.05 s. The stem is nearly exhausted.
5. Noise: 3-seed accuracy std is about 0.15-0.2 pp, and any RNG or step-count change reshuffles it. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: accuracy readings fell below my point when training signal was cut. Time-neutral boosters were over-predicted. E043 showed that rebuilds can shift accuracy by 0.3 pp.

Unsure: whether bandwidth-bound levers transfer to the PCIe judge. Whether padding or a profile-driven systems change gives more than 2%. Whether BN recalibration helps. Averaged weights with stale BN stats could be worth a real gain, but nothing measured here tests it.

forecasts.reason: Costs a little time; the paired gain is unmeasured here. BN stats from lerped fast weights could be stale, but EMA gains so far have been small.
Doubling the step count in the 20 px phase adds per-step overhead for an uncertain gain; 20 px steps are cheap but small batches use the GPU poorly.
Group 2 freeze saves about 1.5% but every training-signal cut so far has cost accuracy, and the tip is already at the bar.
Diagnostic only; no recipe change, so time and accuracy stay at the tip's values, with rebuild noise.
E031 cost about 0.27 pp for 10% fewer steps; a 5% dose should cost about 0.13 pp, which is within noise.
Math-identical, so accuracy is unchanged apart from reshuffle noise. A 24 to 32 channel pad may help or hurt by about 1-2% of time; the saving is uncertain.

cruxes: Does a rebuild or re-run of identical code shift accuracy by about 0.3 pp, as E036 vs E043 suggest? That decides whether any 3-seed keep decision is meaningful.
Does the profile show group-1 conv1 (Cin=24) is inefficient? If so, padding to 32 channels (I073) is the only cheap systems win left.
Does the tip's unselected mean stay at or above about 0.752? If it does not, no further trim can be kept.
